slides.title: Gasoline is fading, but headline CPI only drops in March 2027 data
points: October 2026 pump prices averaged $4.31, under EIA's $4.40
slides.notes: Core, food and other energy are assumptions (trailing 12-month pace). Sources: BLS, EIA.

slides.title: The market already prices a 19 bp rise in the 1.5-year yield
steps: 1.5-year yield if the curve does not move
points: The note wins only if the yield ends below the forward
slides.notes: Forward from the note financed at the bill; cross-checked against the bootstrapped par curve.

slides.title: Weekly gas prices predict next month's CPI print, not gasoline itself
points: A 1:1 rule beat the estimated model, so it is the baseline

slides.title: Expected edge vs the bill: +0.00% if flat gasoline is priced, -0.63% if EIA's forecast is
slides.notes: Left: market prices flat gasoline. Right: market prices EIA's forecast. Scenario yields are assumptions.

slides.title: What would change the call
cards: For a full month, with the 2-year yield not falling: supports the note
Now 4.51%: the entry level with the outlook unchanged
3-month annualized core: argues against the note
slides.notes: Full trigger table in the memo, section 6.
